archetype.name: Field General (point-guard mode)
archetype.definition: A tenth-year passer running Andy Reid's offense on timing and placement, spreading short and intermediate throws around a strong run game instead of living off-script the way he once did.

report.headline: A safer, on-time Mahomes is winning, but his best receivers keep disappearing.
report.take:
This is not the 2018-2022 Mahomes who topped the league in EPA. It is a more controlled version that has looked better than the one from 2023-2025. His aggressiveness has fallen to 7.59%, below even his 2021 low, and well under last year's 13.3%. His throws land about two yards short of the sticks on average. He gets the ball out in 2.71 seconds. The payoff is real: a 3.7% sack rate (6th of 45), a pressure-to-sack rate back down to 19.4% after two years near 27-29%, and fewer bad throws than last season. His EPA per dropback of 0.174 ranks 13th, about the same tier as his last three seasons. His 8.28 yards per attempt (7th) is his best since 2022.

The value comes from two places. First, an efficient underneath game: 0.235 EPA on 0-9 yard throws. Second, a short list of intermediate throws that have been excellent: 0.587 EPA and +10 CPOE on 22 attempts. Travis Kelce (0.725 EPA per target) and Tyquan Thornton (1.269 on 15 targets) produced nearly all of that. The setup helps too. Kansas City has the league's best rushing EPA and the 3rd-ranked defense, so he is rarely in a hole. Under center, where play-action lives, he posts 0.27 EPA per play with +7.1 CPOE.

The season line hides how narrow the base is. Thornton is on injured reserve after ankle surgery and Rashee Rice is out with a hamstring. Xavier Worthy has the most targets on the team (29) and has produced exactly zero EPA on them. Kenneth Walker's 23 targets are slightly negative. The deep ball has been poor: 38.9% completions, two interceptions, no touchdowns on 18 attempts. The middle of the field has been his worst area. All nine touchdown passes came in the red zone, where his per-play EPA is roughly flat. The legs have mostly disappeared as well, down 18.7 rushing yards a game from last season. His fantasy line leans on the 29-point Week 2 and a Week 1 rushing score. Over the last three games he has averaged 14.5 PPR points even as his efficiency rose.

The direction depends on the receivers. With Kelce and the run game, this version of Mahomes can keep winning ugly. Without Thornton, and with Rice out for now, the passing game becomes Kelce plus checkdowns until Worthy shows he can be a real target. Expect efficient, low-variance passing with modest yardage and touchdown totals rather than a return to the 5,000-yard years.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance is back
strengths.body: He is taking a sack on 3.7% of dropbacks, 6th-best among qualifiers. His pressure-to-sack rate of 19.4% is a sharp reversal from 28.8% last year. It comes from the quicker, less aggressive approach: when the first or second read is there he takes it rather than drifting to extend. It matches his 2021-2023 levels, so it looks like a real recovery and not luck. The new tackle injuries will test it.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy, built around Kelce
strengths.body: On 10-19 yard throws he has posted 0.587 EPA per attempt and +10 CPOE, the best part of his game. Kelce at 0.725 EPA per target has been the main outlet over the middle and on the boundary. Twenty-two attempts is a small sample, but Kelce's role is stable. The question is who else gets open at that depth now that Thornton is gone.

strengths.title: Run game makes play-action pay
strengths.body: Kansas City ranks 1st in rushing EPA, and it shows in his under-center numbers: 0.27 EPA per play and +7.1 CPOE, against 0.14 EPA from shotgun. A defense ranked 3rd keeps games neutral, so Reid can stay balanced. This support is structural and should hold as long as the offensive line does.

concerns.title: His most efficient receivers are sidelined
concerns.body: Thornton was the big-play piece at 1.269 EPA per target and is on IR until January. Rice, the other positive wideout, is out this week. What remains outside of Kelce is Worthy, with zero EPA on a team-high 29 targets, and Walker's negative receiving output. This is about the roster, not Mahomes, but it caps what the passing game can do until Rice returns.

concerns.title: Deep and middle throws are leaking
concerns.body: He completes 38.9% of 20-plus-yard throws, with two interceptions and no touchdowns. Throws to the middle have produced two interceptions and -3.1 CPOE. The deep EPA is still positive, so the hits have been big. But the turnovers cluster where defenses can bracket, and losing Thornton removes the receiver who stretched the field. Eighteen attempts is a hint rather than a verdict.

concerns.title: Lower ceiling from the safer style
concerns.body: The trade for fewer sacks is less aggressiveness and almost no rushing: he is down 18.7 rushing yards a game and 5.7 points of aggressiveness from last season. Every touchdown has come in the red zone, where his per-play EPA is near zero. That makes his scoring depend on drives finishing rather than on chunk plays. It is a deliberate choice rather than a flaw, but it is why his recent fantasy output lags his efficiency.

trend.note: His game-by-game passing EPA has swung from -2.3 in Week 1 to 13.4 and 12.9 in Weeks 2-3, then back to 1.7 and 2.8. Over the last three games his rates have risen (0.203 EPA per dropback, +6.9 CPOE), while touchdowns have dropped to 1.33 a game, including none against the Chargers.

nextGame.headline: Stingy Seattle takes away the deep ball; he must live underneath.
nextGame.body:
Seattle has the league's 2nd-ranked defense by EPA. It allows the fewest quarterback passing yards (175.7 a game) and the 2nd-fewest QB fantasy points. It is 3rd against deep throws and 2nd at limiting explosive passes, which takes away the area where he has struggled most anyway. The opening is short: Seattle ranks 24th in EPA allowed on short throws, and his 0-9 yard game has been efficient. The game script points to a slow, grinding night. Seattle's offense ranks 25th, leans on the run despite a 30th-ranked rushing attack, and the total is 42.5 with Kansas City a 2.5-point underdog. That means fewer possessions and fewer chances to pile up volume.

Availability on his side is the real problem. Rice is out and Thornton is on IR, which leaves Kelce, Worthy and Walker as the main targets. Starting tackle Jaylon Moore (89% of snaps) is questionable after a concussion, and Josh Simmons is out. That is a poor setup against a pass rush ranked 2nd in hit rate. On Seattle's side, linebacker Drake Thomas (87% of snaps) is out. That should loosen the underneath zones where Kelce and Walker work, and backs already draw an above-average share of targets against this defense.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle's rush versus patched tackles
keyMatchups.body: Seattle hits quarterbacks at the 2nd-highest rate in the league. Kansas City may be without Moore, and Simmons is out. His quick release and improved pressure-to-sack rate are the counter. If Moore can't go, expect even more quick throws and screens.

keyMatchups.title: Underneath space without Drake Thomas
keyMatchups.body: Seattle is vulnerable short (24th in short EPA) and loses an every-down linebacker. That favors Kelce over the middle and Walker out of the backfield. Backs draw 21.4% of targets against Seattle, compared with 17.7% league-wide. This is the route to a functional passing game.

keyMatchups.title: Low-possession game script
keyMatchups.body: Seattle runs more than the situation predicts and its offense rarely sustains drives. Kansas City's defense is 3rd in EPA. Both teams playing ball-control football points to a low-volume night for him, even if the Chiefs move the ball efficiently.

nextGame.watch: Whether Worthy can turn his targets into positive plays. If he can't, the passing game shrinks to Kelce and checkdowns against the league's best pass defense by yardage.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts of this season that should last are the sack avoidance, the quick, accurate underneath game and the support from a top run game and defense. Those come from approach and roster, not hot streaks. What is less stable is the passing ceiling. Thornton's production is gone for the regular season, so any explosive plays now depend on Rice's return and on Worthy improving. The intermediate efficiency on 22 attempts is likely to cool. The deep interception rate should also settle, mostly because he is likely to throw deep less. Expect something around 230-265 passing yards and 1.3-1.8 touchdowns a game. Weeks with no rushing touchdown and no long scoring throw will feel like the Chargers game.

The low end comes into play if the tackle injuries linger, because his gains against pressure rest partly on protection. The upside case is Rice coming back healthy and becoming a second reliable target beside Kelce. That would bring the intermediate game back closer to its early-season level.
swingFactors: Rashee Rice's hamstring and return timeline
Health of tackles Jaylon Moore and Josh Simmons
Whether Worthy becomes a positive target

confidence.note: Five games, with key splits on under 25 attempts and a receiver group that just lost its two most efficient wideouts.
